We've now explored the whole picture, including the "what happens when" situations, and everything is settled. Here's what we've agreed the app should do — in plain terms:

**Getting in**
- You sign in with an email and password; your bookmarks live in one place so you can reach the same collection from any device.

**Saving**
- Paste a link and its title and description fill in automatically; you can edit them, add tags (typed as chips, reusing tags you've used before), and add your own personal note.
- If a link's details can't be fetched, you can still type a title and save. Junk that isn't a real link can't be saved, and it tells you why.
- If you save something you already have, it doesn't make a duplicate — it takes you to the existing one, ready to edit.

**Finding again (the heart of it)**
- One search box searches titles, descriptions, notes, links and tags, live as you type, across both To read and Finished. Clicking a tag is a quick shortcut.

**Organizing & keeping tidy**
- **To read / Finished** tabs to separate what's left from what's done (nothing deleted).
- **Archive** to hide something from your normal lists but keep it recoverable (and out of normal search).
- **Delete** to remove something for good, with a confirmation.
- Every bookmark is fully editable: web address, title, description, note, tags, and status.

That's **13 settled flows** in total.

**May I now switch from exploring to actually building this app?** Once you say yes, I'll move into development (Phase 2) and design and implement exactly this scope — I won't add or change scope without checking with you.

One heads-up in the interest of honesty: the "reach it from any device" sign-in means I'll build a small central service to hold your account and bookmarks. I'll keep it simple and focused on this scope. Shall I proceed?
